caption:
Every assessment we issue has to survive cross-examination, not just a briefing. That standard shapes how we work before it shapes what we say.

An output that can't be traced back to a specific pass, a specific timestamp, a specific signal, doesn't go out labeled as fact. It goes out labeled as what it is — assessed, not confirmed. In the Numan reach-monitoring run, the flood signature was flagged four days ahead of the official warning. The 2021 control year stayed quiet, correctly, because there was nothing to flag. Both outcomes matter. A system that only reports when told to report isn't proof of anything.

We are not a unit and we do not claim operational history we don't have. We build the evidence trail — imagery, timestamps, revisit logs — so a decision-maker or a court can check our work, not just accept it.
thread: An assessment that can't survive cross-examination doesn't go out labeled as fact. That's the standard we hold ourselves to before anyone else does.
Confirmed. Assessed. Unknown. Every line traced to a pass, a timestamp, a signal — because a claim without a trail is an assertion, not evidence.
Proof point: the Numan reach-monitoring array flagged the 2022 flood signature four days before the official warning. The 2021 control year stayed quiet, correctly.
Both outcomes matter. A system that only speaks up on cue proves nothing about what it does the rest of the time.
We're not a unit and don't claim a service record we don't have. We build the record so it can be checked, not just trusted.

card.headline: Every claim has to survive a check
card.sub: Confirmed. Assessed. Unknown. Evidence traced to a timestamp — not asserted, verified.

rationale: Reframes the mission around methodological accountability (traceable evidence, honest labeling) rather than repeating prior confidence/limits angles, and ties it to the one proven claim without inventing new detections.
